concept: Charged particle in a uniform electric field
prompt:
An electron enters the region between two parallel plates horizontally at $2.0\times10^{7}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The plates are 5.0 cm long and the vertical field is $2.0\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$. ($e=1.6\times10^{-19}$ C, $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg)

**(a)** Calculate the vertical deflection of the electron as it leaves the plates. **[3]**

**(b)** State the shape of its path between the plates. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $a=\dfrac{eE}{m}=3.5\times10^{15}\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ **(A1)**; $t=\dfrac{0.050}{2.0\times10^{7}}=2.5\times10^{-9}$ s **(A1)**; $y=\tfrac12at^{2}=1.1\times10^{-2}$ m **(A1)**

**(b)** A parabola — constant horizontal velocity with constant vertical acceleration, like a projectile **(A1)**

concept: Charged particle in a uniform magnetic field
prompt:
A proton moves at $2.0\times10^{6}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ perpendicular to a uniform 0.20 T magnetic field. ($m_p=1.67\times10^{-27}$ kg)

**(a)** Calculate the radius of its circular path. **[2]**

**(b)** Show that its period does not depend on its speed, and explain why its speed stays constant. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $qvB=\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=0.10$ m **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $T=\dfrac{2\pi r}{v}=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ — no $v$ **(A1)**; the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work **(R1)**

prompt: In a region with perpendicular fields $E=4.0\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$ and $B=0.10$ T, charged particles of a certain speed pass straight through undeflected. Calculate this speed and explain why it is independent of the particles' charge.
markscheme: $qE=qvB\Rightarrow v=\dfrac EB=4.0\times10^{5}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ **(A1)**; both forces are proportional to $q$, so it cancels **(R1)**

concept: Direction of the magnetic force on a charge
prompt: A positive ion moves to the right across the page through a magnetic field directed into the page. The magnetic force on it is:
markscheme: **A.** By the left-hand (or right-hand) rule, $\vec F=q\vec v\times\vec B$ points up the page. An electron would be pushed down.

prompt: A 0.20 m wire carrying 3.0 A lies in a 0.050 T field at $30^{\circ}$ to the field lines. Calculate the force on it and the maximum force for any orientation.

Two long parallel wires 2.0 cm apart carry currents of 5.0 A and 8.0 A in the same direction. ($\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$)

**(a)** Calculate the force per unit length between them. **[2]**

**(b)** State whether the force is attractive or repulsive. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\dfrac FL=\dfrac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi r}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5.0\times8.0}{2\pi\times0.020}$ **(M1)** $=4.0\times10^{-4}\ \text{N m}^{-1}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Attractive (currents in the same direction attract) — and each wire feels the same force, by Newton's third law **(A1)**
